{{Use mdy dates|date=August 2017}} {{Infobox election | election_name = United States House of Representatives elections in Nevada, 2018 | country = Nevada | type = legislative | ongoing = yes | previous_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Nevada, 2016 | previous_year = 2016 | NVxt_election = United States House of Representatives elections in Nevada, 2020 | NVxt_year = 2020 | seats_for_election = All four Nevada seats to the [[United States House of Representatives]] | election_date = {{Start date|2018|11|06}} | party1 = Democratic Party (United States) | last_election1 = 3 | seats1 = | seat_change1 = | popular_vote1 = | percentage1 = | swing1 = | party2 = Republican Party (United States) | last_election2 = 1 | seats2 = | seat_change2 = | popular_vote2 = | percentage2 = | swing2 = }} {{ElectionsNV}} The '''2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Nevada''' will be held on November 6, 2018, to elect the four [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representatives]] from the [[Nevada|State of Nevada]], one from each of the state's four [[Nevada's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with the [[Nevada gubernatorial election, 2018|Nevada gubernatorial election]], as well as [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2018|other elections]] to the [[United States House of Representatives]], [[United States Senate elections, 2018|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[Nevada elections, 2018|state]] and [[United States elections, 2018|local elections]]. Primary elections were held on June 12, 2018.{{cite web|url=http://news3lv.com/news/local/nevada-candidate-filing-begins-monday-primary-is-june-12|title=Nevada candidate filing begins Monday; primary is June 12|first=News 3|last=staff|publisher=|accessdate=June 6, 2018}} {{Toclimit|limit=2}} ==District 1== {{See also|Nevada's 1st congressional district}} Nevada's 1st congressional district occupies the southeastern half of [[Nevada|Nevada's]] largest city, [[Las Vegas, Nevada|Las Vegas]], as well as parts of [[North Las Vegas]] and parts of [[Unincorporated area|unincorporated]] [[Clark County, Nevada|Clark County]]. The incumbent is Democrat [[Dina Titus]], who has represented the district since 2013 and previously represented the 3rd district from 2009 to 2011. She was reelected to a third term with 62% of the vote in 2016. ===Democratic primary=== ====Primary results==== {{Election box begin no change | title = Democratic primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = [[Dina Titus]]''' (incumbent) | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 20897 | percentage = 78.7 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Reuben D'Silva | party = Democratic Party (United States) | votes = 5659 | percentage = 21.3 }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 26556 | percentage = 100.0 }} {{Election box end}} ===Republican primary=== ====Primary results==== {{Election box begin no change | title = Republican primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = Joyce Bentley | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 6444 | percentage = 55.2 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Fred Horne | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 5235 | percentage = 44.8 }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 11679 | percentage = 100.0 }} {{Election box end}} ===General election=== ====Endorsements==== {{Endorsements box | title = Robert Van Strawder (L) | list = ;Musicians * [[Shock G]], rapperhttp://independentpoliticalreport.com/2018/09/digital-undergrounds-shock-g-endorses-robert-strawder-libertarian-for-us-house-nv-1/}} ====Polling==== {| class="wikitable" |- valign= bottom ! It includes most of [[Douglas County, Nevada|Douglas County]] and [[Lyon County, Nevada|Lyon County]], all of [[Churchill County, Nevada|Churchill County]], [[Elko County]], [[Eureka County, Nevada|Eureka County]], [[Humboldt County, Nevada|Humboldt County]], [[Pershing County, Nevada|Pershing County]] and [[Washoe County, Nevada|Washoe County]], as well as the state capital, [[Carson City]]. The largest city in the district is [[Reno]], the state's second largest city. Although the district appears rural, its politics are dominated by Reno and Carson City, which combined cast over 85 percent of the district's vote. The incumbent is Republican [[Mark Amodei]], who has represented the district since 2011. He was reelected to a third full term with 58% of the vote in 2016. Amodei is running for reelection{{cite web|url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2017/may/31/dismissing-statewide-bid-amodei-will-seek-re-elect/|title=Dismissing statewide bid, Amodei will seek re-election The incumbent is Democrat [[Jacky Rosen]], who has represented the district since 2017. She was elected with 47% of the vote in 2016 to replace Republican U.S. Representative [[Joe Heck]], who ran for the U.S. Senate and lost. }} {{Election box end}} ==District 4== {{See also|Nevada's 4th congressional district}} The 4th congressional district was created as a result of the [[2010 United States Census]].{{cite web|url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/thefix/mapping-the-future/red-states-gain-as-new-congres.html|title= Census 2010 shows Red states gaining congressional districts|publisher= Washington Post|accessdate=December 21, 2010}} Located in the central portion of the state, it includes most of northern [[Clark County, Nevada|Clark County]], parts of [[Lyon County, Nevada|Lyon County]], and all of [[Esmeralda County|Esmeralda County]], [[Lincoln County, Nevada|Lincoln County]], [[Mineral County, Nevada|Mineral County]], [[Nye County]] and [[White Pine County]]. More than four-fifths of the district's population lives in Clark County. The incumbent is Democrat [[Ruben Kihuen]], who has represented the district since January 2017. He was elected by defeating incumbent Republican U.S. Representative [[Cresent Hardy]] with 49% of the vote in 2016. In December 2017, Kihuen announced that he would not seek reelection in 2018 following allegations of sexual harassment.{{cite news |last=Viebeck |first=Elise |date=December 16, 2017 |title=Rep. Ruben Kihuen won’t seek reelection amid sexual harassment allegations |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/powerpost/wp/2017/12/16/rep-ruben-kihuen-wont-seek-reelection-amid-sexual-harassment-allegations/ |work=[[Washington Post]] |location=Washngton DC |access-date=December 16, 2017 }} ===Democratic primary=== After incumbent Representative Kihuen announced he would not seek reelection in 2018, the only candidate filed to run against him in the primaries was Amy Vilela. Former U.S. Representative from this district Steven Horsford, who was defeated in the 2014 election, as well as Nevada Legislator Pat Spearman, later announced their plans to run for the Democratic nomination for the seat several months later, due to the opportunity brought about by Kihuen’s announcement. ====Candidates==== ;Declared * John Anzalone, High School Principal * [[Steven Horsford]], former U.S. Representative[http://mcindependentnews.com/2018/01/spearman-jumping-race-replace-kihuen-ex-rep-horsford-nlv-mayor-lee-regent-stephens-considering-bids/ Spearman Jumping into Race to Replace Kihuen; Ex-Rep.
